key_insight: The paper proves that the dimension of a simple connected GHZ graph is bounded by a function of its vertex connectivity, giving a general structural limit on how large a GHZ state can be from such graphs.
engineering_relevance: For quantum-optics and distributed quantum computing, this provides a connectivity-based design rule that helps estimate whether a graph-based photonic setup can generate high-dimensional multipartite GHZ states.
method: Derive an upper bound on GHZ graph dimension using vertex connectivity κ(G).
Extend the analysis to obtain new bounds in terms of edge connectivity and maximum degree.
Connect graph-theoretic connectivity properties to feasible monochromatic inherited vertex colorings.
evidence_signal: The result is theoretical, built from graph-theoretic proofs rather than experimental data, and it sharpens prior partial results for graphs with low connectivity.
watch_item: The bounds apply to simple connected GHZ graphs, so translating them to more general experimental architectures may require additional modeling assumptions.
